claims.text: The funding opportunity offers annual project grants.
The grants support research into the material past.
The research can be in fields such as archaeology, art history, architectural history, material culture, and the history of collecting.
The grants are for projects where the Society will be the main or a significant financial contributor.
The grants support definable objectives with specific, measurable outcomes within larger projects funded from a range of sources.
Applications are welcomed from early career researchers.
Applications are welcomed for projects that are innovative in their approach, entail new initiatives, and/or create interdisciplinary interest.
Applications must be from the project director or principal investigator.
Work contributing to an undergraduate or postgraduate degree is not funded.
Retrospective applications will not be considered.
Travel to, or attendance at, conferences is not funded.
Eligible project costs include travel & subsistence for project team members.
Eligible project costs include costs of specialist or scientific investigation, and of technical services such as imaging and illustration, where these have to be commissioned.
Eligible project costs include hire of plant and site accommodation.
Eligible project costs include materials and consumables.
Eligible project costs include hire of specialist equipment to which the applicant cannot reasonably be expected to have access.
Ineligible project costs include personal remuneration.
Ineligible project costs include salaries of staff holding current appointments.
Ineligible project costs include institutional overheads.
Ineligible project costs include internal hire charges within the applicant’s institution or between project partners.
Ineligible project costs include publication subventions and publication grants (including costs of digital dissemination).
Ineligible project costs include contingency estimates.
Awards are made on an annual basis with possible renewal for up to two further years.
A new application is required each year, and no project will be funded for more than three years.
Projects should not start before April 1st in the year of application.
Grants should be taken up by December 31st of the year in which they are awarded.
The Research Grants scheme is competitive.
Decisions are based on the quality of the research proposal and its viability, both financial and practical.
Decisions consider how the project supports and aligns with the Society’s own strategy and values.
All decisions made by the Committee are final.
Applications will be assessed solely on the basis of the information provided on the application form.
A clear and detailed articulation of research aims and how these will be achieved, with costings and proposed duration, is required.
A clear statement of the contribution of the proposed research to scholarship is required.
A clear plan for the timely publication/dissemination of the results of the research is required.
A request for a specific sum with all applications to other funding bodies declared is required.
A statement of the minimum sum needed to make the project viable in the event of full funding not being obtained is required.
For subsequent applications for the same project, a summary of results to date and a statement of expenditure from the previous grant are required.
Most awards require one or two references.
Applicants are responsible for ensuring references are received by the deadline.
Members of the Research Committee cannot act as referees.
Award recipients must demonstrate they have received all relevant permissions to undertake their project before funds are released.
Any unspent award remainder must be returned for reinvestment.
By February 28th of the year following the award, recipients must submit a report of up to 1,000 words on how research objectives were met.
By February 28th of the year following the award, recipients must submit a financial statement detailing how the Society’s money was spent.
By February 28th of the year following the award, recipients must submit two or three digital images illustrating the project.
No further grant will be made to any applicant who does not meet reporting requirements.
The Society may request short reports for newsletters or website inclusion.
Acknowledgement of the Research Grant in any publication or practical use of the research is required.
Applications for Hugh Phillips, Margaret and Tom Jones, Wainwright Research Archaeology in Wales, and Open Research must be received by January 15th annually.
References for Hugh Phillips, Margaret and Tom Jones, Wainwright Research Archaeology in Wales, and Open Research must be received by January 21st annually.
Applications for Beatrice di Cardi, Janet Arnold, Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler, and William Lambarde must be received by April 7th annually.
References for Beatrice di Cardi, Janet Arnold, Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler, and William Lambarde must be received by April 14th annually.
There are two application rounds for William and Jane Morris Church Conservation grants: March 31st and August 31st annually.
Research Awards offer grants of £500 to £5,000.
Janet Arnold Awards offer grants of £350 to £5,000.
Beatrice de Cardi Awards offer grants of £5,000 to £15,000.
Margaret and Tom Jones Awards offer grants of £1,000 to £10,500.
Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler Travel Awards offer grants of up to £500.
William Lambarde Travel Awards offer grants of up to £500.
William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants are between £500 and £5,000.
Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants are up to £4,000 per project.
